text:
alex: hey everyone :wave: quick question — if i'm hitting a setup problem (vpn/ssh) where should i post? #help? dm eng? also curious about bot noise, how to opt out of some onboarding bots

sam: welcome! :tada: for infra-ish setup, post in #help first. if it's a team-specific token or repo access ping your team channel (e.g., #eng) and @oncall if urgent

maya: devex here — +1 to #help. if you file a ticket also paste the ticket link. To opt out of onboarding bots, go to Settings > Notifications > Apps and mute 'onboarding-bot'

alex: thanks! any quick checks before opening a ticket? vpn or creds tips

ben: try `ssh -v git@github.com` and `ping internal-registry`. Also check SSO page: https://intranet.redwood.dev/ssoconfig

devops-bot: Reminder: For infra incidents, include a snippet of the command and any error logs. Use triple backticks for logs.

alex: got it. how do we do threading etiquette? when do replies belong in-thread vs new message?

sam: short answer: thread the ongoing back-and-forth. If it's a new topic or follow-up that others might search later, start a new message. Always @mention if you need attention from someone not in the thread

maya: example: "Can someone grant repo access?" -> start a new thread in #help so it's indexed. "Thanks, I applied the fix" -> reply in the same thread

lina: onboarding tip: introduce yourself in #random-intros with your role + 1-sentence what you'll work on. People often DM for quick intros after that

alex: perfect, i'll post there. last q: how to reduce bot DMs? they can be noisy

ben: settings -> Apps -> notifications -> uncheck for the specific bot. For channel bots, use `/mute` on the channel or use Do Not Disturb hours

sre-oncall: if you see an automated alert in #incidents, don't reply in-thread unless you're taking action — add a short "taking this" reply and then DM the oncall

alex: awesome, this helps a lot — thanks all :pray:
